title: Create src/lib/tasks/schema.ts with Zod validation
description: Create a Zod schema for the tasks.json format. The schema validates an array of task objects with all required fields. Export both the schema and the inferred TypeScript type.
acceptanceCriteria: Schema validates: id (number), title (string), description (string), category (string), passes (boolean), passCondition (string)
TaskSchema.parse() throws ZodError on invalid input (missing required fields)

steps.details: Create the file with: import { z } from 'zod'. Define the category enum: const CategoryEnum = z.enum(['config', 'functional', 'ui-ux', 'data-model', 'api-endpoint', 'integration', 'security', 'testing', 'docs'])

Create: export const TaskSchema = z.object({ id: z.number().int().positive(), title: z.string().min(1), description: z.string().min(1), category: CategoryEnum, passes: z.boolean(), passCondition: z.string().min(1), blockedReason: z.string().optional() })

steps.description: Define TasksFileSchema for the full file
steps.details: Create: export const TasksFileSchema = z.object({ tasks: z.array(TaskSchema) }). Export the Task type: export type Task = z.infer<typeof TaskSchema>. Export TasksFile type.
In a temporary test script or test file, call TaskSchema.parse() with a valid task object and confirm it returns the parsed value. Then call it with an object missing 'title' and confirm it throws.

technicalNotes: z.enum() creates a union of string literals — add new categories here if the list expands
The TypeScript type is inferred automatically from the Zod schema — no need to define it manually
